limitations: Offline analysis of retained public evidence only; no new chain collection or current balance claim.
Operating-address scope: the two historically linked controllers on BSC, Ethereum and Avalanche. Other candidate custody addresses are not yet included.
Fusion earlier representation history is partial (two captured pages); full-time child excludes dated slices. Never add representation supplies together.
Source histories have explorer discovery limits. Failed/null responses remain diagnostics even where another file supplies a retry.

Exact matching uses same holder, equal deposit/mint amounts or burn/payment differences of 0 or 0.5 BUSD with delay -120 seconds to 24 hours. A second pass uses same-holder burns 0 to 5 minutes before payment, with variable positive differences bounded by 1% of payment and chain-specific caps (BSC 0.5, Avalanche 0.05, Ethereum 50 BUSD). These are candidate-search hypotheses, not verified fee rules.

Migration candidates are same-transaction cross-representation transfers of equal raw amount involving the holder. This is a conservative exclusion from external matching, not a complete migration classification.
Candidate edges are not accepted matches. Many-to-one and one-to-many candidates are explicitly competing; split/batched payouts and different recipient addresses need manual review.
Unmatched means no candidate under these rules and captured coverage, not proof of loss or absence of a burn. Missing timestamp and zero-value movements remain explicit.

Triage flags use configurable 10,000 BUSD and 90% reconstructed-balance-reduction thresholds. They indicate review priority, not misconduct. Reconstructed balances assume zero before the first retained event and are not pinned-state attestations.

Possible asset exchanges require successful receipt context and a net opposite-direction transfer of another token involving the same operating address. This does not prove a swap, valuation, continued custody or replacement backing; native-asset legs without Transfer logs remain uncovered.

A separate short-delay-absolute-fee fallback requires same-holder full-time burns and source payments both receipt-verified, with nonnegative delay at most 60 seconds and unchanged chain absolute fee caps. It does not enforce the 1% relative bound; every such candidate is flagged fee-exceeds-relative-bound. This is a distinct fee hypothesis, not confirmation of redemption. Competing edges remain visible.

reported-asset-exchange requires a same-receipt Swapped event with exact token, participant and amount, or a V2-style Swap event corroborated by both token-transfer legs and its recipient. Event emitters and reported recipients are preserved; this does not authenticate protocol code, independently trace native delivery, link a Fusion burn or establish reserve backing. All exchange classifications retain backing-disposition-unresolved.

A single-relay pool-swap rule follows an equal-amount asset transfer through one intermediate address in the same successful receipt. Exactly two nonzero transfers of that asset may touch the relay, both receipt-verified and correctly ordered; both event IDs are retained. Split, merged or longer routes are not inferred.

An opt-in source-chain pairing hypothesis links still-unmatched, receipt-verified incoming/outgoing asset movements for the same wallet on different chains, with delay 0 to 300 seconds and a nonnegative difference no greater than 50 BUSD and 5% of the deposit. All links and competition remain visible; there is no common bridge identifier and no implication of a Fusion burn or reserve coverage.

Ethereum deposit-fee candidates require both source and Fusion mint receipts, same holder, delay 0 to 300 seconds, a positive deposit-minus-mint difference no greater than 0.05 BUSD and 1% of the source deposit. This bounded-deposit-fee rule is an explicit hypothesis, not an authenticated fee schedule.

Fusion receipt-slice-conversion exclusions require an equal-amount opposite mint/burn for the same holder in a successful receipt, using the configured sibling contracts (all 18 decimals) whose common parent is documented in research/busd-time-slice-coverage.md. Interval supplies are not added together. This is a transaction-purpose classification, not proof of external backing.

Delayed review widens bounded variable/deposit-fee and source-chain hypotheses to 24 hours, without changing normal classifications, counts or unpaired Fusion IDs. New edges are exported separately with competition. Existing exact-fee searches already use 24 hours; absolute-fee fallback remains 60 seconds.

Direct-mint-call and direct-burn-call require successful receipt context, a top-level call to the token or configured parent, the standard mint(address,uint256)/burn(address,uint256) selector, canonical holder and exact amount agreeing with the event. Selectors do not authenticate deployed source. The 12 liquidity-migration-call-candidate mints are a configured target/selector interpretation documented in research/busd-ledger-reconciliation.md and remain eligible for external matching. No direct call or migration-path label establishes external backing.

Controller inventory reviews reconstruct the configured Fusion account/token ledger from retained full-time events with a zero opening balance. A successful burn that clears a nonnegative reconstructed balance is labelled controller-observed-balance-clearing; its preceding inventory events are retained. This is not a settlement match, does not prove economic purpose and does not remove it from unpaired totals.

Payout-address discovery searches unpaired, receipt-verified holder burns against retained source-token transfers and separately labelled explorer-only observations, using existing exact-fee and widened bounded-fee rules. Configured Fusion inventory accounts are routed to their separate review. Unknown senders are candidates only; no operating address is automatically added. Explorer rows have synthetic IDs and no asserted log index, remain outside the ledger and require node corroboration before promotion.

Ethereum and Avalanche discovery retained 74 holder lookups per chain. Uncapped or empty explorer responses do not establish completeness. Bulk BSC discovery remains unavailable from the tested free APIs; one browser inspection does not establish holder-wide coverage.
